subject.title: [Bug]: Cron agent jobs silently time out during sustained LLM API outages instead of fast-failing on definitive errors

question: How should plain provider `api_error: Internal server error` be classified for cron/fallback behavior: `server_error`, `overloaded`, `timeout`, or a cron-local transient that avoids shared auth-profile cooldown?
rationale: The code path shows this is not just a regex gap because each classification changes retry matching, model fallback behavior, and whether shared auth-profile health is affected.

options.title: Use a cron-local outage class
options.body: Treat the plain provider 500 as retryable for cron/fallback without marking shared auth profiles unhealthy unless maintainers explicitly opt in.

options.title: Map it to server_error
options.body: Use the existing structured `server_error` path so cron retry policy and state report server errors consistently while avoiding shared auth-profile cooldown.

options.title: Map it to overloaded
options.body: Skip same-provider profiles sooner through overload cooldown behavior, accepting the risk of poisoning shared provider health during broad HTTP 500 outages.

recommendation.title: Use a cron-local outage class
recommendation.body: Treat the plain provider 500 as retryable for cron/fallback without marking shared auth profiles unhealthy unless maintainers explicitly opt in.

likelyOwner.reason: altaywtf merged the closest structured server-error retry change and is the strongest available routing signal for this classifier/cooldown policy.
